title: The Metal That Remembers Its Shape
hook: A crushed metal wire is expanding right now inside thousands of human hearts.
script: A crushed metal wire is expanding right now inside thousands of human hearts. How can a crumpled piece of metal heal itself the instant it gets warm? This shape memory alloy called nitinol always returns to shape without breaking atomic bonds. A thin cold strand can lift a hundred pounds the second heat hits it. While normal metals soften in fire, heat actually makes this alloy twice as stiff. These metals unfold inside clogged arteries, flexing smoothly with every single heartbeat. It is an inanimate metal behaving like living muscle, remembering who it was.
